editorial:
Imagine stepping back into 1968 and following a man who feels completely out of place in his own life. You get to experience a slow-burn story that focuses on the small, quiet moments of a man trying to find his way through a changing world. The vibe is very relaxed and focuses more on feelings than a big, loud plot. You will spend most of the time just watching the main character deal with his personal struggles, which makes you feel like you are right there in the room with him.

What really works here is the acting, as the lead actor manages to show a lot of emotion without saying much at all. The pacing is quite slow, which might bore some people, but it helps you really get into the mood of the era. If you enjoy old-school cinema that takes its time, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: At the very end, you see the main character finally make a big decision to leave his old life behind. He walks away from the people who held him back and heads toward the coast. There is no huge explosion or shocking twist, but the final shot shows him smiling for the first time. It wraps up by showing that he finally found a sense of peace and freedom on his own terms.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old European films and deep character stories.
